business_scope.primary_industry_name: Laser Micro-Machining of Bioresorbable Vascular Polymer Stents

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Swiss Code of Obligations, cantonal administrative legislation, federal regulatory overlay)

Convention between Switzerland and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing of 10 October 1997 (AMLA; SR 955.0), as amended; Federal Ordinance on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLO; SR 955.01), as amended; Swiss Criminal Code (SCC; SR 311.0), Articles 305bis and 305ter; Swiss Code of Obligations (CO; SR 220), Articles 697j et seq. and Articles 620 et seq.; Swiss Financial Market Supervision Act (FINMASA; SR 956.1).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Country-of-origin national authorities or passport office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin country is party to the Apostille Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization through the Swiss representation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft Articles of Association (Statuts / Statuten) and incorporation resolution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Swiss notary public and founding shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Swiss notarial deed; apostille is not required domestically but may be required if the deed is to be exhibited abroad

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / excerpt from the commercial register of any corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration notice (Meldung der wirtschaftlich berechtigten Person)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and apostille/consular legalization for foreign signatories

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, OFAC, UN, and Swiss domestic sanctions screening of all UBOS, directors, officers, and authorized signatories. Screening must cover the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) embargo and sanctions list, EU restrictive measures transposed into Swiss law, and Swiss MROS financial intelligence references. Enhanced due diligence under AMLA Article 6 and AMLO is mandatory for politically exposed persons, high-risk countries, entities with bearer shares, and complex ownership structures. Records must be retained for at least ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (Zefix.ch) and the competent Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) of the canton of registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be in Latin script and may be expressed in German, French, Italian, or Romansh. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin characters. The corporate form indicator, typically 'AG' or 'SA', must be consistent with the language of the name. A misleading name and a name that duplicates a registered name are not admissible.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Swiss, Suisse, Schweiz, Helvetica, Confoederatio Helvetica
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the Commercial Register Office, the applicant may within 30 days of the written rejection file an administrative appeal to the cantonal Administrative Court (Verwaltungsgericht / Tribunal administratif). The appeal must state the legal grounds and propose an alternative name. Before appealing, the applicant may submit a modified name to the Commercial Register Office without new fees. If the rejection is grounded in denial of prior ministerial or regulatory approval, the applicant may separately request reconsideration from the relevant supervisory authority, such as FINMA, the Federal Office of Public Health, or the cantonal health authority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for this Class III medical device manufacturing company. The registered office must be a physical Swiss address in the canton of incorporation. A virtual office cannot satisfy the statutory registered seat requirement under Swiss Code of Obligations Article 51 and would be rejected by the Commercial Register Office and Swissmedic. Physical premises must support manufacturing, quality control, and regulatory inspection requirements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: estimated 75% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by Swissmedic or the cantonal enforcement authority within the first 18 months of licensing, increasing to over 90% once the manufacturer submits a Class III medical device conformity assessment dossier.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss bank, licensed trust company, or audit firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark confirmation fee for verification of paid-up capital under Swiss Code of Obligations Article 632

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, SR 220), Articles 620-763 (Aktiengesellschaft / societe anonyme); key sections: Art. 621 (minimum share capital CHF 100,000), Art. 629 (notarial deed of incorporation), Art. 632 (paid-up capital and escrow deposit requirement), Arts. 698-706a (general meeting), Arts. 707-726 (board of directors); implementing Commercial Register Ordinance (Handelsregisterverordnung, SR 221.411) Arts. 91-102.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Zug), supervised by the Federal Commercial Register authority of the Swiss Federal Department of Justice and Police (FDJP); electronic filing portal e.um.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public notarial deed of incorporation (Errichtungsurkunde) together with the registered Articles of Association (Statuten), submitted as Form A registration; legal personality arises upon Commercial Register entry with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital for a Swiss AG is CHF 100,000; at least 20% of the nominal value of every share (i.e. minimum CHF 20,000) must be fully paid up in cash at incorporation and evidenced by a bank certificate confirming deposit on a blocked escrow account (Sperrkonto) at a Swiss-regulated bank; funds remain blocked until Commercial Register entry and must be at the free disposal of the board thereafter; any contribution in kind under Art. 628 para 2 CO requires a licensed auditor's formation report.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the shares of the Company are hereby issued and allotted to the founding shareholders against full payment of the statutory paid-up capital of CHF 20,000, such amount being confirmed by the bank certificate of the escrow account and unconditionally available to the Company upon registration; RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is adopted at Baarerstrasse 10, 6300 Zug, Switzerland, and all corporate records shall be kept there; RESOLVED, that Mr. Alexander Keller is appointed Chairman of the Board and Mr. Markus Weber is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each with individual signatory authority, effective as of the Commercial Register entry; RESOLVED, that the Board mandates the registration officers to execute the filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Registration and Intellectual Property Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug and e.um central business-name index (ZEFIX); Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property (IPI) for trademark pre-check.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name-reservation request (Vorabentscheid) to the Zug Commercial Register Office proposing up to three alternative corporate names for CH AG; the register verifies compliance with Arts. 950-951 CO regarding truthfulness, distinctiveness, and the mandatory Aktiengesellschaft/AG suffix; simultaneously run a Swiss trademark and domain conflict search through IPI and the Swiss domain registry; a clean decision letter is required before the notarial deed can be signed.
required_dossiers: Completed e.um name-request form
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten)
Passport or ID copies of the founding shareholders and beneficial owners
IPI trademark-search extract confirming no conflict
Precise statement of corporate purpose covering the manufacture of Class III coronary drug-eluting stents and bioresorbable vascular scaffolds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is objected to because of identity or confusion with an existing registered name, file an amended request with a distinct auxiliary name within ten working days; no re-notarization is required at this stage; a negative decision may be appealed to the Cantonal Commercial Register Supervisory Authority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Escrow Deposit and Bank Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: FINMA-licensed Swiss bank (e.g. Zuger Kantonalbank or UBS Switzerland AG) acting as escrow depositary under Art. 633 CO.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked company account (Sperrkonto) in the name of CH AG in Formation; deposit the minimum paid-up capital of CHF 20,000 representing 20% of the nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 by wire transfer from liquid personal funds; obtain the statutory bank confirmation (Bankbescheinigung) attesting that the funds are at the free disposal of the board after registration; the bank confirmation must be dated no earlier than five working days before the notarial deed execution.
required_dossiers: Escrow account opening application
Draft Articles of Association and founding deed
Founders' identification and source-of-funds declaration under Swiss AML rules (GwG)
Beneficial-owner control forms
Registered agent confirmation of the Zug company address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank imposes an extended AML review, use a notarial escrow (Anderkonto) at the cantonal notary or transfer to an alternative FINMA-licensed bank; document the lawful source of funds before re-deposit; if contribution in kind is proposed, obtain an auditor's formation report and update the bank confirmation accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Deed of Incorporation and Articles Execution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal notary public of Zug (Notariat des Kantons Zug) acting under Art. 629 CO.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders appear before the Zug notary for public authentication of the deed of incorporation and the Articles of Association, including corporate purpose, nominal capital of CHF 100,000, share subscription list, and first board appointments; the notary certifies receipt of the bank confirmation and beneficial-ownership declarations; the authenticated deed is thereafter transmitted to the Commercial Register together with the signature declaration forms.
required_dossiers: Name-reservation decision (Vorabentscheid)
Statutory bank confirmation for CHF 20,000 paid-up capital
Share subscription list signed by all founders
Articles of Association with mandatory clauses under Art. 626 CO
Passport or ID of each founder and each appointed director
Beneficial ownership declaration for financial intermediaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies incomplete or non-compliant clauses, execute a supplementary notarial amendment signed by all founders; foreign founders unable to appear may be represented under a notarized power of attorney with apostille; any defect in the share-subscription or capital-cover statement is cured by correcting the deed and re-executing before the same notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Register Filing and Legal Personality Entry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug with publication in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form A and the notarized deed and statutes electronically through the e.um platform; the registrar examines compliance with the Code of Obligations, the AML ordinance, and public law requirements; upon approval the company acquires legal personality under Art. 643 CO and the Commercial Register Extract (Handelsregisterauszug) and UID number are issued; the entry is published in SHAB.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation
Form A registration application signed by the board
Bank confirmation of paid-up capital
Certified copy of the Articles of Association
Written acceptance declarations of appointed directors and auditors
Beneficial ownership list under GwG
Registered office address confirmation in Zug
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues an interim order (Zwischenverfuegung), respond with corrected documents within thirty calendar days; if registration is refused, file an administrative appeal to the Commercial Register Supervisory Authority and ultimately to the Federal Administrative Court; the SHAB publication follows automatically upon entry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, UID and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) for UID and VAT; Cantonal Tax Office of Zug for corporate income and capital tax; SVA Zentralschweiz for AHV/IV/EO social insurance; SUVA for mandatory accident insurance.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online to the ESTV for the Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer immediately after Commercial Register entry; submit the VAT registration form if expected annual taxable turnover exceeds CHF 100,000 or electively; open an employer file with the SVA compensation office for wage-based AHV deductions; register with SUVA for the medical-device manufacturing risk tariff; respond to the Zug Tax Office notice of interim capital and profit tax installments.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register Extract (Handelsregisterauszug)
UID application and VAT registration form (Formular 1301)
AHV employer registration declaration
Lease agreement of the Zug registered office
Board minutes confirming commencement of business
Projected profit-and-loss and opening balance sheet for cantonal tax assessment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT decision is delayed, invoke ex-officio registration under the Swiss VAT Act and request a written confirmation; if the cantonal tax office sets an unreasonably high interim payment, submit a revised lower forecast before the first assessment; any late AHV registration is cured by immediate filing with payment of minimal arrears interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Swissmedic, Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products (Schweizerisches Heilmittelinstitut), Department of Medical Devices, with operational coordination by the Health Office of the Canton of Zug (Gesundheitsamt Kanton Zug) and SUVA for workplace safety.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Swissmedic Manufacturing Authorisation for Medical Devices (Herstellungsbewilligung fuer Medizinprodukte) under Art. 48 in conjunction with Art. 51 of the Medical Devices Ordinance (MedDO, SR 812.213), together with ISO 13485 quality management system certification and GMP compliance for Class III coronary drug-eluting stents containing an active pharmaceutical substance.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Swiss Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN/BAFU), implemented by the Office for Environmental Protection of the Canton of Zug (Amt fuer Umweltschutz Kanton Zug).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 preliminary environmental screening and registration, not a full EIA under Art. 10 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (BUPA), provided annual solvent throughput remains below 150 tonnes and wastewater loads stay within GSchV limit values; a full EIA would be triggered only for large chemical operations or substance volumes exceeding specified step-6 thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater per Swiss Water Protection Ordinance (GSchV, SR 814.201) Annex 3.2 para 41: pH 6.5-9.0, COD no greater than 20 mg/L, TOC no greater than 15 mg/L, AOX no greater than 0.1 mg/L, total suspended solids no greater than 20 mg/L, active drug-substance concentration below the PNEC for the receiving water; exhaust air per Clean Air Ordinance (LRV, SR 814.318.142.1) Art. 32: VOC mass flow no greater than 1.5 kg/h and total carbon concentration no greater than 75 mg/m3; hazardous waste handling per the Movement of Waste Ordinance (VVVA) with traceable consignment notes; laser-generated particulates filtered through HEPA H13 with removal efficiency of at least 99.97%.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety approval by the Zug fire prevention authority covering solvent storage, EX-zone electrical classification, and an automatic extinguishing system; structural load and vibration-attenuation inspection of the cleanroom facility by the Zug building inspectorate (Bauinspektorat Kanton Zug); occupational clearance under SUVA including appointment of a laser safety officer, workplace hygiene monitoring for isopropyl alcohol and acetonitrile vapours, and medical surveillance of cleanroom personnel.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung, ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions, AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni, AIC) and its mandatory E-VAT portal at www.estv.admin.ch; cantonal tax administrations are separately responsible for cantonal and communal corporate income/capital tax registration in the canton of the registered office (e.g., Zug, Zurich).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity that conducts taxable supplies in Switzerland and exceeds the Swiss VAT registration threshold must file an application with the ESTV/FTA using the official E-VAT electronic portal (ISiTax). If the foreign entity has no domestic seat, it must designate a VAT representative residing or established in Switzerland. The application must identify the governing corporate form (e.g., foreign stock company equivalent to Aktiengesellschaft), intended activity, projected turnover, and effective date of liability. Upon approval, the FTA assigns a nine-digit VAT identification number in the form CHE-XXX.XXX.XXX (RFC/MWST/TVA/IVA). The UID-CH business identification number from the Federal Statistical Office is integrated for tax-administrative purposes. Registration with the cantonal tax administration for corporate income/capital tax is done via the Swiss Central Compensation Office or the cantonal portal; distinct cantonal company tax numbers are issued separately.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Swiss law provides no US-style check-the-box election. Available statutory elections include VAT group registration (Steuergruppe), corporate income tax group/fiscal unity under Art. 62 DBG, application of the participation exemption for qualifying dividend and capital-gain income, notional interest deduction on excess equity (notioneller Zinsabzug), R&D super-deduction of 150% in certain cantons, election to allocate costs under the transaction-based method for transfer pricing, and the option for cross-border B2B services to be treated as received at the recipient's place of establishment for VAT purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 (annual turnover from taxable supplies; for a non-resident foreign entity, CHF 100,000 of taxable supplies made within Switzerland unless the supplies are already exempt or only subject to VAT at a reduced rate under special provisions)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time government fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime for domestic VAT. Electronic invoicing (QR-bill, eBill, EDI, PDF/A) is legally recognised and permitted, but the exporter must retain the original data in an unaltered, integrity-protected format for 10 years. There is no API-based mandatory clearance with the FTA for each invoice; the FTA may require that electronic invoices incorporate a verifiable authenticity and integrity mechanism (e.g., advanced electronic signature, hash, or secured EDI transmission). Statutory invoice particulars include supplier name and VAT ID, recipient, date, type and quantity of good, consideration, applicable rate, and VAT amount. Absence of the mandatory particulars for export documentation renders the zero rating invalid.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero rating is available under Art. 23 VATA for the supply of goods that are physically exported from Switzerland by the supplier or on its behalf, including goods delivered into bonded warehouses or customs-free zones, provided the export takes place before first use/enjoyment in Switzerland and the supplier obtains verifiable proof of export. For services, zero rating applies when the place of supply is located abroad (B2B reverse-charge rules), but physically exportable goods in the drug-eluting stent value chain require a Swiss customs export declaration. The stent manufacturer must demonstrate the transport chain from Swiss territory to the foreign destination; subcontract cooling chain or logistics service documentation must be preserved.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (Ausfuhrzollanmeldung / déclaration en douane d'exportation) confirmed by the Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (BAZG/FOCBS)
Commercial invoice and sales contract containing export terms, product description, ISIC/HS classification, and foreign buyer reference
Transport document (Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR letter of conveyance) proving physical removal of the goods from Switzerland
Certificate of arrival / customs-entry evidence issued by the destination-country customs authority where required by FTA audit practice for high-risk medical exports
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 credit advice evidencing payment from the foreign buyer where the FTA or the bank requires corroboration of the export transaction
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The FTA will disallow the 0% rate and re-render the export taxable retroactively if the customs declaration is deficient, the transport evidence is incomplete, or the exporter fails to substantiate actual departure from Switzerland. Re-rendering triggers additional VAT at 8.1%, default interest at 4.5% per annum, and administrative fines under Art. 96/97 MWSTG. In cases of intentional tax evasion, the fine may reach CHF 100,000; fraudulent or deliberately misleading zero-rating claims may attract criminal pecuniary penalties and imprisonment up to three years under general criminal tax law. Unjustly retained input VAT is clawed back in full, and the limitation period for reassessment is 10 years in cases of tax evasion; all export and customs records must be retained for this period.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the Swiss State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) for financial market policy; no separate foreign exchange administration exists, as Switzerland maintains a unitary monetary authority framework
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Switzerland has full current and capital account convertibility under the Swiss Federal Constitution and the Federal Act on the Free Movement of Capital; no general exchange control restrictions exist on profit remittance, dividends, or repatriation of capital for Swiss-resident Aktiengesellschaft companies; however, the SNB retains the right to introduce temporary safeguard measures in the event of severe currency distortion, and banks impose enhanced due diligence for high-risk medical device manufacturers. Profit repatriation is subject solely to Swiss withholding tax at 35% on dividends unless reduced by double taxation treaty or Swiss participation relief; no prior regulatory approval is required for outbound remittances if anti-money laundering declarations and tax compliance declarations are in order
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists under Swiss law; export receipts may be retained in foreign currency or converted at the exporter's discretion; Swiss banks follow FINMA circular 2011/1 regarding the clarification of the legal framework for the holding of foreign currencies; no mandatory conversion ratio applies, and the Swiss National Bank does not enforce any obligation to exchange export earnings into CHF

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Credit Suisse AG (now integrated within UBS Group legal entity structure)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury clearing because Swiss law does not grant full banking licenses to electronic money institutions for commercial lending or complex cross-border Class III MedTech operational accounts; FINMA-regulated fintech licenses (fintech licence under Art. 1b of the Swiss Banking Act) permit deposit-taking up to CHF 100 million on an interest-free basis but do not cover letter of credit issuance, export factoring, or complex multi-currency treasury settlements. Offshore EMIs such as those licensed under the UK FCA or Lithuanian LB may operate only as payment initiation or account information service providers under the Swiss Payment Services Act (PSA) and cannot hold client funds in Switzerland without a Swiss banking license; practical viability is restricted to ancillary pre-funded disbursement wallets, with all main liquidity clearing executed via SWIFT members.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For corporate accounts of a Swiss Aktiengesellschaft with high-risk MedTech classification, Swiss anti-money laundering legislation (AMLA, FINMA Circular 2016/07) requires the bank to establish the identity of the beneficial owner, the economic purpose of the account, and the source of funds; in practice all tier-1 Swiss banks mandate an in-person introduction or onboarding interview of at least one director with signatory authority, typically a board member or CFO, before account activation. Where the director is a non-resident, remote opening is generally not available for a CHF-denominated corporate account with international payment traffic; video identification is accepted only after a face-to-face meeting with a bank officer or a recognized Swiss diplomatic/notarial agent. Cantonal banks such as ZKB and BCV occasionally allow remote initial documentation review for Swiss-incorporated companies if a local trustee or fiduciary holds a notarized power of attorney, but final sign-off requires physical presence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk sector classification under FINMA Circular 2016/07 Annex 1: medical device manufacturing with export exposure and third-party intermediaries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized articles of association; certified trade register excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug) dated within 90 days; evidence of valid Swiss therapeutic products license from Swissmedic; CE marking certification under EU MDR 2017/745; ISO 13485 certificate; proof of physical office operations in Switzerland; organizational chart with ultimate beneficial owners and their source of wealth declarations; business plan detailing stent manufacturing, distribution channels, and expected transaction counterparties

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or shareholders in jurisdictions perceived as tax-optimization or secrecy environments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Individual KYC file for each non-resident director/UBO: passport copy certified by a Swiss notary; police clearance certificate issued within 6 months; reference letter from a regulated bank in the director's home jurisdiction; tax residence certificate; sworn declaration of no adverse regulatory history; corporate registry extracts for intermediate holding entities disclosing the full ownership chain until a natural person

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected high-volume cross-border wire traffic with sharp invoice patterns potentially indicating trade-based money laundering
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Execute letters of intent and master supply agreements with EU/US hospital distributors detailing pricing mechanics; validate supply chain through Swissmedic import/export certificates; invoice template with unique pro-forma numbering, Incoterms 2020 terms, and stated provenance of medical polymers; monthly treasury forecast with counterparty onboarding files including sanctions screening output from OFAC and SECO; presentation of audited financial statements or a sworn accountant declaration for early-stage entity

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow account funded by loans from shareholders rather than equity subscriptions, creating ambiguity under Art. 634 Swiss Code of Obligations rules on capital contributions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder loan facility agreements with clear market-rate interest or subordination clauses; bank confirmation certifying the source of transferred funds; board resolution approving the loan and capital contribution timetable; an independent Swiss fiduciary audit opinion concluding that funds are not derived from criminal proceeds and that CHF 100,000 minimum capital will be fully paid before capital increase registration

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of holding-company chaperone structures involving Zug crypto-era intermediaries for treasury routing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete ownership and control narrative for all intermediary vehicles; notification under Swiss AMLA Art. 8 identifying any intermediary as a financial intermediary regulated by FINMA; evidence of professional status of each chamber/provider as a licensed Swiss fiduciary with due diligence reports; copies of outsourced compliance functions, if any, under the Swiss Financial Institutions Act

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections and shareholder loans must be effected via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 through the Swiss SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) system with a clear payment purpose code. For equity capital contributions, remittance should reference purpose code 'P04 – Capital contribution / equity participation' and the bank must receive a copy of the notarized capital increase resolution and the Swiss commercial register deposit confirmation. For shareholder loans, use purpose code 'P03 – Loans between non-financial enterprises' or OECD purpose category '810 – Financial loans' depending on the sending bank's classification; no exchange control approval is required. Banks will verify that the foreign payer is the same entity or beneficial owner as recorded in the Swiss registers, and large cash amounts or payments from unregulated money-service businesses will be rejected. For payments exceeding CHF 100,000, Swiss banks must comply with the DBA (Duty to report suspicious financial activity) under the AMLA and may require a written explanation of the corporate purpose. For a Class III stent manufacturer, inbound funding from strategic foreign healthcare investors must include the clinical trial validation milestone schedule and the corresponding intellectual property valuation to satisfy enhanced KYC.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for coronary stent materials and finished device sales will be cleared primarily through three rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 single payment credit transfers for distributor settlements and supply-chain prepayments where risk terms are 30-90 days open account; (2) SWIFT MT700/MT707 commercial letter of credit issuance or confirmation for large Latin American and Southeast Asian hospital tenders, enabling exporters to obtain documentary protection through a Swiss advising bank; and (3) the Swiss SIC real-time gross settlement system for CHF-denominated domestic counterparty payments. The LC instruments must include a compliance clause stating the beneficiary bank is SWIFT-connected and that goods are classified under HS code 9021.40 (cardiovascular devices, including coronary stents). For each MT103, the payment must reference the underlying invoice number and include either purpose code 'B2P' (business-to-business payment) or the ISO 20022 structured remittance reference, satisfying the Swiss banks' obligation to perform transaction monitoring. Sanctions screening through OFAC, SECO, and EU sanctions lists is mandatory for every outbound payment; payments into high-risk jurisdictions require submission of an end-user certificate and a pre-shipment export authorization from the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) if the stent contains controlled semiconductor micro-machining inputs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: plain-vanilla over-the-counter forward contracts (USD/CHF, EUR/CHF, CNY/CHF) with Swiss or EU/UK banking counterparties under ISDA 2002 master agreements
nondeliverable forwards (NDF) on CNY, INR, BRL and IDR for hedging emerging-market receivables where local currency convertibility restrictions prevent physical settlement
cross-currency swaps between CHF and USD or EUR for long-term refinancing of intra-group loans, executed on a cleared basis through LCH SwapClear or bilateral under ISDA CSA
FX options (European style) for protection of tender-based distributor contracts, subject to FINMA market conduct rules and to the eligibility requirements of the counterparty

currency call accounts and transactional conversion orders placed with the Swiss clearing bank for natural hedging of daily operational flows, under an approved treasury policy limiting tenor to under 12 months

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income and capital tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal Tax Administration (Kantonssteueramt) and Federal Tax Administration (ESTV)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the business year end (June 30) for federal tax with extensions granted by the canton; cantonal deadlines vary between March 31 and June 30 initially
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest of 4.5% per annum from the due assessment date; late filing penalty of 1–10% of assessed tax; escalation fines up to CHF 5,000; eventual enforced collection with asset seizure and administrative dissolution if the company remains insolvent

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and audit report submitted to the Annual General Meeting (AGM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Meeting of Shareholders of the AG; public filing required only for companies with listed debt securities or where statutes require publication
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: AGM must be held within 6 months after the balance sheet date (31 December for standard calendar year); adoption of annual accounts by ordinary resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Board liability for failure to convene AGM; administrative warning from Commercial Register Office; possible judicial order convening the AGM; loss of discharge from liability and exposure to director claims

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value-added tax return (or quarterly VAT return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of each quarterly VAT period; small-scale annual settlement is possible with annual return due within 60 days after calendar year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 4.5% per annum; payment reminder surcharges up to 1% of tax; administrative fine up to CHF 10,000 for futile warnings; prosecution for willful tax evasion up to triple tax value

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual AHV/AVS old-age and survivors' insurance wage declaration with contribution settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Social Security Compensation Office (Ausgleichskasse) and AHV/AVS contributions central clearing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly interim declarations per payroll; annual wage declaration due by 15 February of the following year for full-year settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compensation interest at 5% per annum on overdue contributions; warning surcharge of 10–20% of unpaid contribution amount; criminal fines for late filing of wage declaration, up to CHF 30,000 in aggravated cases

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual board statutory register audit and event-driven commercial register notification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Register Office of the Canton of Zug (Zuger Handelsregisteramt) / Federal Commercial Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuously during the year; no annual filing required unless board changes, share capital changes, audited events, or articles of amendment occur; such changes must be filed promptly after the relevant resolution
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Compulsory-fine procedure (Ungehorsamstrafe) against defaulting officers; commercial register office can strike off association if no legal address or no functioning board; fine up to CHF 10,000 for breach of filing duty; loss of statutory protection against third-party reliance

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Full ordinary audit (Ordentliche Revision) is compulsory for a stock corporation when, during two consecutive years, two of the following thresholds are exceeded: CHF 20 million in total assets, CHF 40 million in turnover, 250 full-time employees on annual average. Simplified audit (Eingeschränkte Revision) is mandatory for all other AGs above the opt-out threshold. Opting-out from the audit office is allowed only if the company does not exceed 10 full-time employees on annual average and all shareholders give their unanimous written or EGM consent.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Swiss statutory accounts prepared under the Swiss Code of Obligations (OR) articles 957–963, equivalent to Swiss GAAP FER; consolidated financial statements under IFRS if the AG is a securities issuer; IFRS or Swiss GAAP FER accepted for individual annual financial statements where applied consistently.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss company law does not require a separate beneficial ownership declaration to a central registry on an annual basis. The AG must maintain continuous internal registers of shareholders and beneficial owners (under the AMLA for non-listed AGs), and at each AGM the shareholders formally confirm the ordinary capital structure and profit appropriation. Any transfer of registered shares is effective upon entry in the share register, and notification to the commercial register is required only for acquisitions of major shareholdings that occur during the year; a procedural confirmation at year-end serves as the annual reconciliation of these registrations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Verwaltungsratsverzeichnis / Record of Board Members)
Minute Book (Protokollbuch / Minutes of Board and AGM Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200 – 4,500 annually for registered office and administrative support services in Zug or Zurich for a non-operating AG; 4,500 – 12,000 for full corporate secretarial outsourcing with compliance monitoring
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,200 – 24,000 for simplified audit (Eingeschränkte Revision) of a lower-revenue medtech manufacturing AG; USD 25,000 – 90,000 for full ordinary audit at or above the statutory thresholds, dependent on inventory, revenue contracts and international related-party transactions

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 8.5% Swiss federal direct corporate income tax (statutory rate computed on after-tax profit; effective pre-tax burden 7.83%); aggregate federal plus cantonal plus communal ordinary corporate income tax rate normally 11.9%–21.0% depending on canton (Zug approx. 11.9%; Zurich approx. 19.7%; Geneva approx. 14.0%).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Swiss Tax Reform and AHV Financing (STAF, 2020) incentives: (a) patent box with exemption of up to 90% of qualifying IP income subject to the nexus approach; (b) additional R&D super-deduction of 50% for qualifying Swiss R&D labour costs; (c) notional interest deduction (NID) on excess equity permitted in certain cantons; (d) participation relief exempting 100% of qualifying dividend and capital-gain income on substantial participations (10% or greater shareholding or market value above CHF 1 million); (e) capital-tax reduction on equity issued or held for patent-box qualifying IP assets.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formular A / Déclaration d'impôt pour personnes morales (combined federal, cantonal and communal corporate income tax and capital tax return); electronic filing through the cantonal tax administration portals (eTax, TaxOnline, Vade or equivalent) under the Swiss Company Register UID (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx); the cantonal tax administration collects and assesses both cantonal and federal direct tax, remitting the federal portion to the Federal Tax Administration (ESTV).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The corporate tax return must be submitted within 6 months after the fiscal year end; for calendar-year companies the cantonal deadline is commonly set between 31 March and 30 June of the following year; extensions up to a further 6 months are available upon written request; non-compliance results in a final mandatory 30-day term (peremptory).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Official company name, registered seat, Swiss UID and trade register number, legal form (Aktiengesellschaft), date of incorporation, fiscal year end.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Swiss AG as a licensed Class III MedTech manufacturer must file the annual return even when 100% of the shares are held by a PRC parent; appoint a Swiss-resident person with power of attorney to sign; attach Swissmedic device licence evidence in annex.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory net profit or loss per management accounts, reconciled to Swiss GAAP FER; this is the starting point for all tax adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only the profit of the Swiss legal entity; intercompany transactions with the PRC manufacturing affiliate (stent cost, royalties, service fees) must be at arm's length and supported by an up-to-date transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: B.2 – Hidden Reserves and Tax Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs of undisclosed reserves, excessive depreciation, non-deductible capital losses, write-offs of goodwill or notional expenses; recognition of previously taxed replacement reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Goodwill booked on the purchase of the stent asset base must be amortised tax-neutral only to the extent economically justified; fines, bribes and excessive representation expenses are non-deductible per Art. 58 DBG.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exemption of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from substantial participations (holding period 12 months; participation of at least 10% of share capital or market value of at least CHF 1 million).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from the PRC subsidiary are exempt from Swiss corporate income tax but foreign withholding tax is not creditable under the participation system; substantiate the effective holding with the Chinese commercial register extract.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduction of taxable income from patented inventions (e.g., bioresorbable polymer stent technology) by up to 90%; additional 50% deduction of qualifying Swiss R&D wages.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The drug-eluting stent patent must be legally owned and economically used by the Swiss AG; contract R&D carried out in China does not qualify except under the statutory outsourcing limits (nexus approach); maintain the nexus-ratio computation and patent register evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: C.1 – Equity Subject to Capital Tax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cantonal/communal capital tax base on shareholders' equity, including paid-up share capital, statutory capital reserves and retained earnings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident ownership does not change the tax base; the Swiss AG must report the fully paid-in minimum capital of CHF 100,000 with an issued capital of at least CHF 100,000 and paid-up part of CHF 50,000 per Swiss company law (Art. 621 CO).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Set-off of prior-year tax losses against current taxable income; maximum 7-year carryforward; no carryback.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only losses incurred and booked by the Swiss AG are usable; losses of a PRC branch or of a Chinese sister company cannot be transferred to the Swiss tax return; loss schedules must show year-by-year utilisation.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine (Ordnungsstrafe) of CHF 50–10,000 per offence under Art. 174 DBG and cantonal equivalents; default interest at 4% p.a. on federal tax and up to 5% cantonal; if the return is not delivered, the tax authority issues a discretionary assessment (tatsächliche Veranlagung) giving the taxpayer no deduction and no loss carryforward; intentionally false declarations constitute tax evasion with fines up to 100% of evaded tax and criminal prosecution of the signing directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 35% Swiss withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer, Art. 1 VStG) on every profit distribution, constructive dividend, and on interest-free loans or excessive licence payments to shareholders where recharacterised as distribution of profit; for a Swiss AG distributing a dividend to its PRC parent, 35% is initially withheld and then partially refunded under the DTA refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Switzerland operates a refund procedure rather than relief at source: the foreign shareholder must file Form 820 (Rückerstattungsgesuch / refund application) with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) within three years of the end of the calendar year in which the dividend was paid, attaching a tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the Chinese State Taxation Administration; the beneficial owner test must be satisfied — the Chinese company must be the ultimate owner and economically entitled to the dividend. The PRC–Switzerland DTA (Art. 10(2)(a)) grants a 5% WHT only if the beneficial owner is a company which holds directly at least 25% of the capital of the Swiss payer; otherwise the rate is 10%. Attach the share register, declaration of chain of title, UBO confirmation and Swiss assessment notice of the payer.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Swiss WHT: 35% on interest from Swiss taxable bonds and money-market instruments only; ordinary bank interest, trade receivables and intercompany cash-pool interest are outside the Swiss WHT net unless structured as debt-like equity or recharacterised as constructive dividends. Royalties: no statutory Swiss WHT on outbound royalties (0% domestic law), but the PRC–Switzerland DTA allows the PRC as source state to levy 10% WHT on licence/royalty payments to a Swiss Swiss-resident licensee, while Swiss internal payments of royalties to a non-resident licensor are free of Swiss WHT; standard DTA rates with main partners: dividends 5-15%, interest 0-10%, royalties 0-10% (US: 0% interest and 0% royalties, 5-15% dividends; Germany: 5% dividends, 5% interest, 5% royalties; China: 5-10% dividends, 10% interest, 10% royalties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File and Master File under the Swiss TP documentation regulation (SR 642.123) once consolidated group turnover exceeds CHF 80 million in a year and the Swiss entity carries out cross-border transactions with related parties; Country-by-Country Report required at consolidated group turnover of CHF 900 million. Below the CHF 80 million threshold, a full TP study is not formally prescribed but is commercially indispensable for a Swiss principal/licence-holder manufacturing Class III stent products, since ESTV audit practice requires a transactional benchmark (typically TNMM) whenever intercompany flows involve IP, procurement or distribution.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland does not apply an explicit Economic Substance Regulations statute as in the UAE/EU, but enforces an equivalent substance doctrine: a Swiss AG must be effectively managed and administered in Switzerland — board meetings in Swiss territory, a Swiss-resident authorised officer, a physical office, and personnel commensurate with the functions performed. The patent box is available only where a substantial part of the qualifying R&D was performed in Switzerland (nexus approach). A letterbox company that merely holds stent IP licences or collects royalties while decision-making occurs in Shanghai or Shenzhen will be denied treaty benefits under the beneficial-ownership rule, may be re-attributed as a permanent establishment of the Chinese parent, and will trigger retrospective reassessments; the historically privileged domicile-company regime was abolished in 2020.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / False Corporate Tax Return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting a Swiss Form A return in which intercompany stent prices are manipulated (under-invoicing export sales to the PRC distribution affiliate, overstating purchase prices from the Chinese manufacturing sister company, or concealing income booked on parallel accounts), intentionally destroying the transfer pricing file, or omitting taxable reserves.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to 100% of the evaded federal tax and equivalent cantonal fine (Art. 175 DBG), default interest at 4%, unlimited reassessment within the 10-year absolute prescription period (20 years for false documents); the fine is not covered by insurance and is personally payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil: the signatories and directors are prosecuted individually for tax evasion; imprisonment up to 3 years applies in hard cases; the cantonal prosecutor may impose a travel ban, asset freeze, and passport revocation; the AG cannot indemnify its directors for criminal fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to withhold and remit the 35% Swiss WHT on declared dividends or on constructive distributions: e.g., paying excessive royalties to a PRC sister group for an asset which in substance belongs to the Swiss AG; granting an interest-free shareholder loan; waiving licence receivables owed by the Chinese parent; or effecting a share buy-back without tax clearance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Swiss AG as debtor company remains liable for the 35% WHT plus 4% interest under the Swiss Withholding Tax Act (VStG), payable within 30 days of the distribution; the DTA refund for the Chinese parent is forfeited if the Swiss company did not withhold; repeated default leads to coercive fines of up to 10% of the unpaid amount.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly refrain from withholding become joint personal debtors for the withheld amount; seizure of personal assets in Switzerland is available; intentional fraudulent withholding or attempted DTA fraud is a criminal offence under the VStG with imprisonment up to 3 years, irrespective of the corporate veil.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance / Money Laundering
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a Swiss AG as a letterbox denomination for Chinese-manufactured coronary stents without Swiss employees, laboratory, quality management or board substance; routing letter-of-credit and SWIFT wire proceeds through Swiss bank accounts with rapid onward transfers to PRC accounts; failure to register the beneficial owner (UBO) in the Swiss transparency register, or falsifying UBO declarations to banks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty refunds and retrospective tax assessments with interest; money laundering under Art. 305bis of the Swiss Criminal Code carries imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to CHF 5 million (CHF 10 million in severe cases); confiscation of the full proceeds under Arts. 70–73 SCC; Swissmedic withdrawal of the Class III device licence; banks close the CHF account and freeze assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Prima facie evidence of unlawful activity: the corporate veil is entirely pierced; directors, fiduciaries and providing attorneys face pre-trial detention and travel bans; they are liable for unpaid social-insurance debts under Art. 52 AHVV and for civil damages for the full unpaid tax, with a prohibition from acting as directors for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an international transaction with the related Chinese stent manufacturer without a Local File and Master File despite group turnover above CHF 80 million; allocating residual profit entirely offshore while the Swiss AG retains entrepreneurial risk; absence of a benchmark study for the stent royalty; charging the Swiss principal a routine cost-plus below the normal TNMM range; or refusing to provide documentation during an ESTV audit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Upward adjustment of the Swiss taxable profit by the ESTV recharacterising the excess royalty or margin as a hidden dividend; supplementary assessment of 35% WHT and 4% interest on the deemed distribution to the Chinese parent; in the case of intentional inadequate documentation, penalty tax up to 100% of the evaded amount (Art. 175 DBG in conjunction with Art. 58a DBG).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign mispriced intercompany contracts are jointly liable for civil damages to the company for the full tax difference under the Swiss Code of Obligations; criminal liability falls on members of the board and the finance officer; because the directors are domiciled in Switzerland, asset seizures and travel bans are enforceable; individual directors cannot invoke the corporate shield.
